analyzed_vuln.description: The subset() method builds an iterator of substituted glyph pairs, maps both sides through glyph_map, and then unconditionally calls SingleSubst_serialize(c->serializer, it) even when the mapped iterator contains invalid / out-of-range glyph IDs. During serialization, CoverageFormat2_4::serialize() writes rangeRecord.arrayZ[range].last = g (CoverageFormat2.hh:106), which stores attacker-controlled mapped values into serialized IntType fields; with malformed GSUB data this leads to a write through an invalid destination object (crash observed at IntType::operator= in hb-open-type.hh:65). Root cause is missing validation/sanitization of mapped substitution pairs before serialization in SingleSubstFormat2_4::subset (crash manifests in IntType assignment).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger via hb-subset-fuzzer with a malformed font containing a GSUB SingleSubst Format2 subtable. Data flow: fuzz input -> hb_subset_or_fail -> GSUB lookup/subtable dispatch -> SingleSubstFormat2_4::subset(). The PoV must produce substitution pairs that survive the two glyphset filters but map via glyph_map to bad/inconsistent coverage/substitute data, so serialize path reaches CoverageFormat2_4::serialize and performs write to invalid memory while filling rangeRecord.arrayZ.

--- a/src/OT/Layout/GSUB/SingleSubstFormat2.hh
+++ b/src/OT/Layout/GSUB/SingleSubstFormat2.hh
@@ -161,6 +161,8 @@
     | hb_filter (glyphset, hb_second)
     | hb_map_retains_sorting ([&] (hb_pair_t<hb_codepoint_t, const typename Types::HBGlyphID &> p) -> hb_codepoint_pair_t
                               { return hb_pair (glyph_map[p.first], glyph_map[p.second]); })
+    | hb_filter ([&] (const hb_codepoint_pair_t &p)
+                 { return p.first != HB_MAP_VALUE_INVALID && p.second != HB_MAP_VALUE_INVALID; })
     ;
 
     bool ret = bool (it);
